learnings.lora_submission: CRITICAL: Cannot submit LoRA adapters directly. vLLM expects full model with config.json. Must merge LoRA into base model before upload.
learnings.submission_format: HF repo must contain: config.json, model*.safetensors, tokenizer files. Not just adapter files.
learnings.hf_repo_tag_required: CRITICAL: Must specify --hf-repo-tag 'main' (NOT --hf-revision). Without it, AIcrowd passes revision=null causing 404 error. Check starter kit docs FIRST.
learnings.chat_template_jinja_override: CRITICAL: chat_template.jinja file OVERRIDES tokenizer_config.json chat_template. ALWAYS check for .jinja files in HF repo and ensure they have correct system prompt. Test locally with force_download=True before submitting.
learnings.test_before_submit: MANDATORY: Run local model test to verify (1) correct system prompt in generated prompt, (2) model outputs <uci_move> tags. One 5-minute local test saves multiple failed submissions.
learnings.vllm_eos_token: CRITICAL: vLLM reads eos_token from tokenizer_config.json, NOT generation_config.json. For ChatML models, must set eos_token to <|im_end|> in tokenizer_config.json.
learnings.neuron_qwen_concurrency_bug: CRITICAL: Qwen models on Neuron vLLM have corrupted outputs at high concurrency. FIX: Add --vllm.max-num-seqs 1 to submission. See: https://discourse.aicrowd.com/t/possible-evaluator-change-concurrency-now-4-was-1-qwen3-neuron-vllm-outputs-corrupted-finish-reason-length-missing-uci-move/17687

sf_depth20_analysis.purpose: Create ultra-high-quality backup data for V7 if V6 plateaus

top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.insight: 77.8% of elite training data already matches SF top-1 at depth 20
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.detail: The existing training_elite_30k dataset is ALREADY high quality. Only 22.2% of positions have human moves that disagree with SF's absolute best. This suggests the elite filtering process is effective - most elite GMs play SF top-1 moves.
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.action: Consider whether stricter filtering is even necessary - 77.8% agreement is strong

top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.insight: Depth 20 vs depth 12 has minimal impact on top-1 filtering
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.detail: At depth 12 with top-3 criterion, ~70% acceptance rate. At depth 20 with top-1 only, 77.8% acceptance. The difference (7.8pp) is LESS than expected. This suggests move rankings are stable between depth 12-20 for most positions.
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.action: Depth 20 filtering may not be worth 4x computational cost for marginal quality improvement

top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.insight: ~22% of elite GM moves disagree with SF depth 20 top-1
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.detail: These 222 positions are WHERE THE MODEL LEARNS WRONG MOVES. They represent human moves that are good (top-3) but not optimal. For chess purists, removing these creates perfect training data. But human-like play may actually benefit from this diversity.
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.action: Two strategies: (A) Train on pure SF top-1 for optimal play, or (B) Keep top-3 for human-like diversity

top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.insight: Processing speed: 2.07 positions/second at depth 20 with 2 workers
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.detail: Depth 20 analysis takes ~0.5 sec/position per worker. Full 30k dataset would take ~4 hours with 2 workers. Scalable but not fast.
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.action: For full dataset filtering, use cloud compute with more workers

top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.insight: SF score enrichment reveals evaluation confidence
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.detail: Each filtered position now includes SF's centipawn score at depth 20. This enables training curriculum sorted by position clarity - train on clear positions first (|score| > 200cp), then nuanced positions.
top_5_insights_jensen_t5t.action: Use sf_score for curriculum learning: easy-to-hard position ordering

sf_depth20_analysis.recommendation: The 778 ultra-high-quality positions are ready for V7 backup training. However, the marginal benefit over existing elite data may be small. Primary V7 improvement should come from endgame augmentation and quiet position training rather than stricter filtering.

comparison_to_baseline.interpretation: Counterintuitively, stricter depth+criterion yielded HIGHER acceptance. This is because elite data was already well-filtered, and depth 20 agrees with depth 12 in most cases.
